title: The city where a jail cell saved one man 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
Would you have stayed in Saint-Pierre? 👇

On May 8, 1902, Mount Pelée on Martinique sent a glowing cloud of gas and ash over Saint-Pierre. About 28,000 people died in minutes. One of the few survivors was a prisoner in a stone cell.

Sources: Wikipedia, "1902 eruption of Mount Pelée" and "Ludger Sylbaris"; EARTH Magazine, "Benchmarks: May 8, 1902: The deadly eruption of Mount Pelée" (2015); Scientific American, "May 8, 1902: La Pelée".

scenes.text: A city of 28,000 people vanished in under a minute.
Saint-Pierre, Martinique, May 8, 1902. Mount Pelée sent a glowing cloud of gas downhill at over 100 mph.
The telegraph operator's last message went out at 7:52. Then the line went dead.
Ships in the harbor burned, including the liner Roraima.
In a stone cell with no windows, prisoner Ludger Sylbaris was badly burned, but alive.
Barnum & Bailey later billed him as the man who lived through Doomsday.
